Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently attended the Startup School 2026 event, and her talk video has now been uploaded to the Y Combinator YouTube channel, as you can see below.

Susan Kare shares wonderful stories and design insights

It has been over 40 years since the original Macintosh was released, but the system's graphics, fonts, icons, and overall UI elements still shine just as brightly as they did back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh are still preserved in macOS today, both in spirit and in letter. From the Command key symbol, the smiling Mac at startup, the system fonts, the hand cursor, and more, Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac, but also influenced personal computer design across the entire industry.

Anyone who has learned a bit about Apple's history has likely seen Kare's sketches, and has read or heard interviews about that early work. But hearing her tell those passionate and frustrating days in person always carries a special meaning — after all, in those days, graphical user interfaces and pixel graphics were still completely uncharted territory.

For that very reason, if you are interested in design, Apple history, or simply enjoy hearing people talk at length with expertise about subjects they love and have devoted their lives to, Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to detailing her work at Apple, Kare also discussed how she joined the company, showed her work after leaving, shared little stories from Apple's early days, and quoted other legendary designers to provide extra inspiration.
